# About the Author {.unnumbered}

**Vijay Janapa Reddi** is the Gordon McKay Professor of Electrical Engineering at Harvard University and a Visiting Professor at ETH Zurich in the Integrated Systems Laboratory (IIS), D-ITET.

His research sits at the intersection of computer architecture, machine learning systems, and edge robotics. Over the past decade, his work has focused on democratizing applied machine learning systems by connecting first-principles silicon constraints to accessible, open-source education—from founding MLPerf and edge benchmark standards to authoring foundational open-source curricula in TinyML and Machine Learning Systems.

---

## The Teaching Philosophy: Zero Magic

From TinyML to MLSys to Physical AI Systems, the pedagogy is anchored in three non-negotiable principles:

1. **Hardware as Pedagogy, Not an Afterthought:** Abstract concepts become permanent understanding only when learners see physical phenomena on the bench with their own eyes—measuring a latency tail on an oscilloscope, watching a motor stall under thermal derating, or observing a microcontroller hardware watchdog catch a Linux kernel crash.
2. **Accessible Rigor:** Every high-level abstraction is traced down to its physical mechanism—clock cycles, DMA channels, memory buses, and mechanical inertia—with explicit interface contracts and zero hand-waving.
3. **One Public Standard:** There is no separate "elite syllabus" or "dumbed-down self-study track." Enrolled university cohorts at ETH Zurich, open-source self-learners, and industrial systems builders follow the exact same curriculum, textbook, and laboratory contracts.

---

## The Kit and Laboratory Development

The hands-on bench laboratories and the reference hardware platform (**The TinyAgents Kit on Arduino UNO Q Dual-Brain**) accompanying this book are developed and maintained in collaboration with **Andrea**, postdoctoral researcher in the Integrated Systems Laboratory at ETH Zurich. 

The lab track translates the architectural contracts and design dossier milestones established in this book into reproducible, bench-verified firmware and software checkpoints for students and practitioners worldwide.
